facts: On September 3, 2026, Mobileye's board designated Chief Operating Officer Yaacov Kobi Ohayon as the company's principal operating officer and as an executive officer for Section 16 purposes.
Ohayon has served as COO of the Mobileye organization since 2020 and has been employed by the company and subsidiaries since 2017; the filing says his responsibilities expanded over time.

The board stated that the designation recognizes the scope of Ohayon's existing responsibilities and does not change his duties, responsibilities, employment status or existing compensation arrangements.
Mobileye's current investor-relations events page lists the Evercore 9th Annual ADAS, AV & AI Forum for September 29, 2026 at 9:40 AM EDT and provides a webcast link.
This converts the previously disclosed September 29 event from a date-only planned appearance into a scheduled webcast event with an exact time.

factors.name: governancePower
factors.basis: The board's formal principal-operating-officer designation clarifies operating accountability around a long-tenured COO without changing duties or compensation; it improves role clarity but does not resolve Intel controlling-shareholder concentration or the separate CEO succession question.

factors.name: executionMonitoring
factors.basis: The September 29 ADAS/AV/AI forum now has a precise webcast time, creating a near-term observable checkpoint for management commentary on operating execution and strategic priorities.

risks.risk: The principal-operating-officer designation is a formal recognition of existing responsibilities rather than evidence of improved operating performance; it should not be treated as an execution result.
The September 29 webcast may contain no material new operating information and should remain a monitoring event rather than a guaranteed catalyst.

contradictions: Formalizing the COO as principal operating officer improves accountability visibility but does not itself answer the previously documented leadership-transition uncertainty or controlling-shareholder governance risk.
unknowns: The filing does not state whether the principal-operating-officer designation changes decision rights in practice beyond formal Section 16 treatment.
The substance and materiality of the September 29 webcast are not yet known.
